Breakfast And After School Club
Breakfast And After School Club
Breakfast Club drop off
Here at Aerodrome Primary Academy, we provide a Breakfast Club and After School Club available for all children from Reception to Year 6. (If your child is in Nursery and you would like them to attend they must have an older sibling attending at the same time.)
Our goal is to provide all children within our care with a happy, safe, caring and stimulating environment before and after school.
The Breakfast Club is open Monday to Friday 7:45am to 8:45am and the Afterschool Club 3:15pm to 6:30pm, term time only (excluding inset days)
Before you can start using our Afterschool Club you need to complete a booking form indicating the days you require. If there are no spaces available for your selected days, you will be added to a waiting list.
No booking is needed to book for our Breakfast Club, we ask if you can put the correct amount on the breakfast club service on ParentPay.
Please find costings on document below. Payments are due by the last day of the calendar month a month prior. If full payment is not received on time, we reserve the right to withdraw your child’s place. You will get an invoice the week before your payment is due. You are not charged for school holidays, bank holidays or inset training days.
If you have credit at the end of the academic year, this can be either refunded at your request or left as a credit towards the following academic year fees.
Per Session After School Club - £14.00
Per Session After School Club Adhoc (one off session) - £15.00
Per Session Breakfast Club - £5.00

Headteacher's Welcome
Aspire, Persevere, Achieve
Welcome to Aerodrome Primary Academy; a vibrant and exciting learning community.
We are so pleased that you are taking an active interest in our school and encourage you to read further and to book a visit to come and see our vision in practice!
At Aerodrome Primary we strive relentlessly to ensure that all our children enjoy a stimulating and diverse education, are fully active in their learning and achieve to the very best of their ability.
High standards and engagement in learning are the main priorities for the staff and children. We aim for high standards in everything; learning, behaviour, attitudes and commitment whilst ensuring children are excited by their learning opportunities. Our vibrant and welcoming learning environment, both inside and outside, provides the children with an inspiring and welcoming space where they have the freedom and support to develop mentally and physically.
Self-drive is a key skill that we aim to foster in all our learners at Aerodrome. Our personalised curriculum ‘Contexts for Learning’ allows both teachers and children alike to identify and develop their interests within and beyond the parameters of the National Curriculum and to take an active role in developing their own learning journeys.
Children are encouraged to share and utilise their ideas and opinions both in the classroom and within the wider school context. Children in the Early Years and beyond are taught and encouraged to make positive behaviour and learning choices that enable them to flourish.
We aim to develop a learning community where children respect each other and take responsibility for their own behaviour and progress. Our whole school ethos is based on understanding and modelling the values that are essential to developing a harmonious and cohesive learning community.
Developing excellent home school partnerships is a first priority when children join our school. We encourage regular contact between class teachers and parents and will happily meet with parents both informally and by appointment to ensure we develop positive relationships that fully support the children in our care.
Our curriculum is enriched by learning beyond the classroom and the children have many opportunities to enjoy school visits, we also welcome visitors into our school to enhance the curriculum. Outdoor learning and a wide range of extracurricular clubs also provide extended learning experiences for all our children.
We value working in partnerships and have developed an active partnership with ReACH2 academy trust, working with and contributing to the development of schools with a focus on learning from each other.
We'd love to welcome you to our school; visits are encouraged so please make an appointment with us so that we can show you around.
Mrs Zoe Foulsham - Headteacher

Admission Appeals
Admission Appeals
Key stage 1 appeals
The law states that infant classes must be limited to a maximum of 30 children which has an impact on how an appeal is considered. An appeal for a reception place can only be upheld in very limited circumstances.
There are 3 circumstances which an appeal panel can uphold an appeal for a school; if an appeal does not satisfy any of these conditions then it cannot be upheld.
These conditions are:
Deadlines for completing online appeal forms
Appeals for Croydon community primary schools and the non-community schools/academies listed below must be completed online. Visit Croydon Website here for more information.
Appeals Timetable in accordance with the School Admissions Appeal Code 2012
Community Primary admission appeals to be heard between 8 June 2020 and 21 July 2020
a) Deadline for Lodging Appeals: 19 May 2020. Appeal forms received within the deadline (19 May 2020) will be heard between 8 June 2020 and 21 July 2020. (i.e. within 40 school days of the deadline)
b) Appellants will receive at least 10 school days’ notice of their appeal hearing date.
c) Appellants must submit their additional evidence and the admission authority to submit their evidence at least 12 school days prior to the hearing date.
d) Wherever possible decision letters will be sent to appellants within 5 school days oft he hearing, or, where multiple appeals for a school are heard on more than one day within 5 school days of the last hearing day for that school.
Notice date: 15 January 2020

Enhanced Learning Provision for Developmental Language Disorder
Entry Criteria and How to Apply for a Place
Our ELP is a specialist provision specifically for children with a diagnosis of Developmental Language Disorder. These are specially funded placements which are offered to identified children from across the borough. Entry is decided via a specialist admissions panel and, occasionally, EHCP consultations (if we are not full and the child meets the entry criteria). We are strictly limited to 20 places and children from our mainstream school do not access this provision or the speech therapy within it.
If you are interested in applying for a place at our ELP, you must discuss this with your current SENCo or SEN caseworker. Please note that the ELP is a provision for children with Developmental Language Disorder. Applicants must meet the Catalise criteria for DLD which is:
‘Developmental Language Disorder’ (DLD) for when the language disorder is NOT associated with a known biomedical condition such as:
 acquired epileptic aphasia in childhood,
 certain neurodegenerative conditions,
 genetic conditions such as Down syndrome,
 sensori-neural hearing loss.
 autism spectrum disorder (ASD)
 intellectual disability

Welcome to Kingfishers and Swans!
Meet the staff in Kingfishers and Swans
Kingfishers and Swans Homework
Kingfishers and Swans Spring Context
Kingfishers context for the Spring term is 'Opposites Attract'.
We will be learning all about polar and desert climates and animals, we even have our very own Arctic corner in our classroom!
We will be looking at hot and cold colours and create a piece of artwork in the style of Ted Harrison.
We will be looking at different types of weather and making a kite to fly on a windy day.
We will be visiting Croydon library and Wing Yip to celebrate Chinese new year. An exciting term ahead!
In Swans we have another exciting term ahead filled with lots of fun learning. This starts with a trip to Beddington Park where we will go fishing in the river and take part in a boat race.
In Science, Swans will be learning about forces through a range of fun and practical experiments.
The children will enjoy art lessons and learn how to sketch bridges and rivers. Using photographs and observations from the trip they will study shapes, lines and features of different bridges.
In Design and Technology the children will work together to share ideas, solve problems and think carefully about which design would make the strongest bridge. Lots to look forward to!

It is expected that on days where your child is not wearing their PE kit that they wear correct school uniform.
Each week the children will receive spellings and times tables appropriate to their level. These will be in the children's homework books each week. Please send in children's homework books on a Tuesday and they will be sent out again on a Thursday with the spellings and times tables for the following week.

We welcome you to the Year 2 Information Page!
Throughout the Autumn Term we will be looking at a new context called 'Who Cares?'
Within this context we will learn about the range of people that care for us. This will include our families and friends and professions that can care for us. We will learn about what it means to be a good friend and which qualities will be needed. Our learning will be a journey through how we can care for others as well as ourselves. In History we will study the Great Fire of London and the plague. Our DT and Art learning will be centered around healthy eating and famous artists who have used fruits and vegetables within their work. Our Science focus will be on exercise as well as animals and their habitats. In RE we will study a range of religions, exploring how we are special. This will be such an exciting term of learning :)

Additional learning at home
You can always carry on your learning, even when at home! Make sure you read for 10 minutes each day and then record it in your yellow reading record books to show your teachers!
Maths is also all around you! Can you count the steps in your house? Add together door numbers? Measure and weigh food/items when cooking?
Always practise your 2,5, and 10 times tables too!

We are all problem solvers!
Every single person is born with an innate level of problem-solving ability.
Early on as a species on this planet, we solved problems like recognising faces we know, protecting ourselves against other species, and as babies the problem of getting food (by crying relentlessly until we were fed).
Why then, if we have this innate ability, does actually teaching problem solving seem so hard?
Mathematical problem solving is a learned skill.
Colin Foster (2019), a reader in Mathematics Education in the Mathematics Education Centre at Loughborough University, says,
‘I think of fluency and mathematical reasoning, not as ends in themselves, but as means to support pupils in the most important goal of all: solving problems.’

Entry Criteria for the Enhanced Learning Provision (ELP) for DLD
Our ELP is a specialist provision specifically for children with a diagnosis of Developmental Language Disorder. These are specially funded placements which are offered to identified children from across the borough. Entry is decided via a specialist admissions panel and, occasionally, EHCP consultations (if we are not full and the child meets the entry criteria). We are strictly limited to 20 places and children from our mainstream school do not access this provision or the speech therapy within it.
If you are interested in applying for a place at our ELP, you must discuss this with your current SENCo or SEN caseworker. Please note that the ELP is a provision for children with Developmental Language Disorder. Applicants must meet the Catalise criteria for DLD which is:
‘Developmental Language Disorder’ (DLD) for when the language disorder is NOT associated with a known biomedical condition such as:
 acquired epileptic aphasia in childhood,
 certain neurodegenerative conditions,
 genetic conditions such as Down syndrome,
 sensori-neural hearing loss.
 autism spectrum disorder (ASD)
 intellectual disability
Pupil Learning Plans (PLP) for children with SEND
Some children will receive a PLP with personal targets for them to achieve.
With this in mind, the class teacher will set and review targets three times a year and share them with parents at parents evening.
We allow for a handover between classes and for the teachers to get to know the children in their class. For Autumn term parents evening, the teachers will review the targets that were set in the Summer term and set new targets. These targets will last until the Spring term and will be reviewed in time for parents evening.
The Autumn targets will be reviewed by the teachers and new targets will be set. This happens after the February half term and the new and reviewed targets are shared with parents at parents evening.
The Spring targets will be reviewed by the teachers and new targets will be set. This happens after the May half term and the new and reviewed targets are shared with parents at the report feedback parents evening or sent home. These targets are carried over until the Autumn term parents evening.
